- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–10% relative to prior 30d trend.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+15% from prior 18d mean), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overreaction.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 30d moving avg), model frequently fails to adjust; add 1–3% downward bias to next 7d forecast.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (e.g., -0.3 to 0.3), model often underestimates downside risk; add 2–5% buffer for potential drop in next 10d.
- If true outcome deviates >10% from 30d forecast in first 3–5 days, model is likely lagging; adjust forecast to align with recent 18d history, not 30d.
- For events with high volatility (e.g., policy change, auction results), model often overreacts; apply 1–3% dampening to forecast if sentiment is uncertain or event is ambiguous.
